slides.slide_title: Introduce /θ/ — mirror work mandatory (5 minutes minimum)
slides.teacher_cue: New sound — voiceless th. HIGHEST PRIORITY KOREAN INTERFERENCE. Korean substitutes /t/ — producing 'tink' for 'think', 'tumb' for 'thumb'. Mandatory 5-minute mirror session before any word work. Tongue tip between the teeth — you should see it in a mirror. Blow gently. No voicing. Contrast: /t/ — tongue stays behind teeth, one burst. /θ/ — tongue tip between teeth, air flows continuously.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /θ/ with tongue tip visibly between teeth and continuous airflow, no voicing.
slides.correction_move: Mirror session: Step 1 — produce /t/, confirm tongue behind teeth. Step 2 — produce /θ/, confirm tongue tip between teeth. Step 3 — alternate t-θ-t-θ until students control the distinction.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /t/ substitution throughout. This is the single most persistent Korean interference error in English. Do not proceed to word practice until isolation production is secure.

slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.

slides.teacher_cue: Say thin — not thick. Confirm tongue between teeth before revealing print. Blend.

slides.correction_move: Model thin orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /t/ substitution. Redirect with mirror if needed.

slides.correction_move: Model think orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /t/ substitution — think is one of the most commonly mispronounced words for Korean learners.

slides.observation_note: Watch for /t/ at the end and for the rounded /ɒ/ vowel.

slides.teacher_cue: Say broth — a thin soup. Note br onset and th coda. Confirm /θ/ at end. Reveal print and blend.
